authorization: User decision 2026-09-20: address the root cause behind SFS falling below the external prefill-TPS estimator at 8.3 QPS in the MLP predictor arms.
diagnosis: SFS admits by simulating each candidate wait, and that simulation consumes predicted output lengths; the prefill-TPS estimator uses prompt tokens and measured prefill throughput only. Swapping in the MLP length predictor (6% worse held-out MAE: 235 vs 222 tokens) tripled SFS wait-prediction error on the 8.3 cell (119 ms canonical -> 338 ms), moved 8B share from 27.0% to 34.8% and cost 7.5 points of TTFT attainment (93.6% -> 86.1%), while prefill-TPS held 90.8%. The fill removes the predictor from the simulated backlog of already-admitted requests, so if this is the mechanism, SFS should recover at 8.3 without losing 7 or 8.
reading: A cell is a win only if it beats the prefill_tps_ontimeutility it repeats; 7 and 8 QPS are the no-regression controls. Any adoption of this fill applies to every SFS cell of the campaign and is reported as the configuration, never chosen per cell.

remaining_length.note: The canonical rule, tables and quantile, applied to every Qwen engine instead of the 0.6B alone: a running request contributes its measured survival-quantile remaining length for its prompt bin, so the simulated decode backlog no longer depends on the output-length predictor for requests already admitted. The tables are the committed ones, built from canonical calibration outputs; nothing else changes.

canonical_arm: The same fill under the canonical predictors. Adopting the fill campaign-wide would re-measure the headline Qwen grid, and the canonical configuration currently benefits from the LightGBM length predictor underpredicting (0.55 predicted/actual tokens), which holds the engine decode reserve down. If the fill costs the canonical grid, adopting it only where it helps would be selection after the fact; this arm measures that before any adoption decision.

results_so_far.reading: Five of six beat the prefill-TPS value they repeat; qwen-mlp_quality-hard-8.3 (0.4688) stays below 0.4865.

flash_arm: Under the Flash judge the flash-trained arm is the one place an external baseline still leads SFS: Mooncake 0.5620 against 0.5505 at 7 QPS. The same fill took the canonical arm scored under Flash from 0.5581 to 0.5890 at that rate, so this measures whether it closes the gap in the arm whose predictor is itself flash-trained. 8 and 8.3 are the no-regression controls.
